chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, who said:

When the time for an obligatory salat (prayer) begins, then there is no supererogatory prayer. As for the manner of making up missed prayers, we have devoted a separate chapter to it immediately after this chapter.

key_terms.الْقَضَاءِ: making up a missed devotional act
key_terms.صَلَاةٍ: salat (prayer), here referring to the ritual prayer
key_terms.وَقْتُ: the appointed time or onset of a prescribed act of worship

ai.seo_question: Can one perform voluntary prayer after the time of an obligatory salat (prayer) has begun?
ai.summary: This report states that when the time of an obligatory salat (prayer) enters, voluntary prayer is set aside in favor of the prescribed prayer. It also indicates that the details of making up missed acts are treated separately, highlighting a juristic concern with proper ordering and priority in worship.
